basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/AmIBeingPwned/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [Am I Being Pwned](https://amibeingpwned.com/) solution for Microsoft Sentinel ingests browser extension security events from Am I Being Pwned: issue alerts about risky extensions, detections of malicious extensions across the fleet, and removals of the Am I Being Pwned browser agent from devices. Analytic rules turn urgent alerts, widespread malicious extensions and agent removals into incidents, and a workbook summarizes alerts, top extensions and agent removals. **Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:** This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in [Preview](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs: a. [Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework](https://aka.ms/Sentinel-CCP_Platform) **Data Connectors:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 3, **Hunting Queries:** 4 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for Am I Being Pwned (via Codeless Connector Framework). You can get Am I Being Pwned (via Codeless Connector Framework) data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
Alerts over time by tier, the extensions with the most alerts and recent browser agent removals from Am I Being Pwned.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

Raises an incident for every urgent issue alert from Am I Being Pwned. An urgent alert means a risky browser extension needs attention now, for example an extension that can steal logins is still running in the fleet, or a block that was sent is not taking effect. Each alert id produces one Microsoft Sentinel alert.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: AIBP - Browser agent removed from device

options.text: Fires when the Am I Being Pwned browser agent is removed from a device. Once the agent is gone, the browser extensions on that device are no longer inventoried or rated, so a removal can hide a malicious extension. Confirm the removal was expected (device retired or reimaged) with the device owner.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: AIBP - Malicious extension detected on many devices

options.text: Fires when Am I Being Pwned reports a malicious or unanalyzable browser extension with at least 10 installs across the fleet, either when it is first detected or when a later alert about it shows the higher count. A widely installed bad extension is a fleet-wide exposure rather than a single-device problem. Adjust InstallThreshold to suit the size of your fleet.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: AIBP - Extensions that steal logins or run remote code

options.text: Lists browser extensions Am I Being Pwned alerted on that can steal logins or run remote code, with their latest state and install count. Use it to find extensions that are still running after a block was sent. This hunting query depends on AmIBeingPwnedEventsConnector data connector (AIBPEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: AIBP - Browser agent removed soon after enrollment

options.text: Finds users whose Am I Being Pwned browser agent was removed within 7 days of enrolling, or removed more than once. A user who keeps removing the agent may be avoiding extension monitoring. This hunting query depends on AmIBeingPwnedEventsConnector data connector (AIBPEvents_CL Parser or Table)

Finds browser extensions that Am I Being Pwned alerted on in the last day and that run for five or more users. One risky extension on many people's machines in a day is usually a campaign or a bad update, not one user's choice. This hunting query depends on AmIBeingPwnedEventsConnector data connector (AIBPEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery4
elements.label: AIBP - Browser agent removed after an alert

options.text: Finds machines whose Am I Being Pwned browser agent was removed within a day of an alert about an extension on that machine. Removing the agent stops extension monitoring there, so right after an alert it can mean someone is avoiding the response. This hunting query depends on AmIBeingPwnedEventsConnector data connector (AIBPEvents_CL Parser or Table)
